transcript: Today, my boyfriend Paul and I saw MTC's production of Poor Yella Rednecks at New York City Center. It’s about a woman and a man who both came to the United States from Vietnam as refugees trying to navigate life together in Arkansas. Poor Yella Rednecks is a family story, an immigrant story, and a story of being Asian in America. It’s described as a comedy but it definitely had some serious moments as well and the tone of the piece was a little all over the place for me. Something else that I didn't expect is that the characters frequently break into rap during the piece? which I thought was… a choice. Overall, I think the piece had some really great moments and is definitely a necessary, impactful story to tell but I felt like it was executed with mixed results, particularly the pacing and some of the musical elements. With that, another playbill for my collection.
